record.title: First 14 turbines in Datang Zhongwei's Chang Le wind project connect and generate
record.summary: China Energy Engineering Corporation reports that on 2026-10-05 the first 14 turbines in the first section of Datang Zhongwei's Chang Le 500-MW wind project completed energization and grid connection and generated successfully. The builder says 75 turbines are planned for the segment and links it to the Zhongwei compute campus. This is a partial commissioning milestone; the report provides no interval generation or campus-delivery data.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: China Energy Engineering Corporation published a project-builder report on 2026-10-10 stating that the first 14 turbines in the first section of the Chang Le project completed energization and grid connection and generated successfully on 2026-10-05.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The builder report identifies the segment as a 500-MW wind project intended to supply the Datang Zhongwei Cloud Base data center and says 75 turbines are planned.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The report does not establish sustained output, commissioning of the other turbines or the broader wind portfolio, delivery to the data center, or realized cost, reliability, emissions or compute-service effects.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent grid/operator confirmation and interval records for the first 14 turbines and subsequent units are unavailable.
Actual delivery from the wind segment to the compute campus, alongside grid imports, storage and outages, is unmeasured in the inspected source.
No realized delivered-price comparison, reliability effect or emissions intensity per useful compute output is reported.

brief.importance_rationale: If sustained, bringing the first 14 turbines online in a 500-MW wind segment intended to supply a compute campus is a meaningful local milestone for electricity procurement and infrastructure planning. The source reports successful commissioning but gives no metered generation, campus delivery, cost or reliability results, limiting the consequence established so far.
limitations: The sole directly inspected source is the project builder's own report; no independent grid record or operator meter data were inspected.
Only the first 14 turbines are reported as connected and successfully generating; the remaining 61 planned units and the wider 1.5-GW wind portfolio are not established as commissioned.
No interval generation, curtailment, storage dispatch, grid exchange, campus receipt, delivered price or matched counterfactual is available.
The builder's projected annual supply and environmental-equivalence figures are contingent on project completion and are not observed outcomes; they are excluded from the supported result.
No energy-use or quality-qualified compute denominator supports an inference about the project's effect on AI service economics or emissions per unit of useful compute.

technical.claimed_result: The builder reports first-stage energization, grid connection and successful generation. No independent measurement is provided.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official builder published the dated commissioning report. the research desk did not verify turbine output, remaining project completion or delivery to the campus.
technical.mechanism: A dedicated wind segment is being built as part of a compute-campus green-power supply project. The builder reports successful energization and grid connection for the first 14 turbines; the available evidence does not quantify continuing generation or end-use delivery.
technical.regime: One project-builder announcement about the first section of a named 500-MW segment; 14 turbines of 75 planned were reported connected and generating on 2026-10-05.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline or measured power-cost/reliability comparison was reported or inspected; therefore no comparative effect is claimed.

brief.title: First 14 turbines in Datang Zhongwei's Chang Le wind project connect and generate
brief.why_it_matters: Power supply is becoming a design constraint for large compute campuses. This builder-reported milestone shows an early wind segment entering generation in a project intended to serve a major compute base, making the physical build worth tracking. Fourteen turbines are only the first portion of a 75-turbine segment, and the available source does not demonstrate sustained electricity delivery or an economic or reliability effect.

related.summary: Distinct project milestone: the related record covers first turbines in the separate Chang Le wind segment; this record covers the earlier 500-MW PV phase.

other.title: Datang’s Zhongwei compute campus solar phase is reported operational; wind supply remains unverified
other.summary: A report hosted by the National Energy Administration’s Northwest Office says China Datang’s 500-MW photovoltaic plant for the Zhongwei Cloud Base entered operation on 2026-05-02. It describes a dedicated-line physical-supply arrangement for incremental data-center load and bilateral power-market transactions for existing load. The article says the separate 1.5-GW wind phase was planned for full grid connection in September 2026 and that 2.29 TWh per year could meet campus demand after the first phase is fully operational. These are attributed project reports; this review did not establish post-September wind commissioning, metered generation, campus delivery or realized cost and reliability effects.
